title: Pinecone 2.0 — Edo Liberty, Pinecone
talk_summary: Edo Liberty argues agents are like brilliant new hires who lack persistent 'tribal knowledge' about the company, and proposes a separate 'knowledge layer' (Nexus) that maintains curated context (markdown, SQL, vector, graph) driven by a declarative manifest. The key mechanism is a 'runtime coding agent' that writes and executes code at query time instead of exposing many tools, cutting prompt tokens from ~150k to <1k and improving cost, speed, and accuracy.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of hand-writing skills/plugins/markdown for agents, you declare in a manifest what tasks, entities, and info you care about, and the layer itself organizes and maintains the underlying files, tables, vector index, and graph.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You tell the knowledge layer, you tell Nexus what you care about in a manifest... it's the knowledge layer's work to keep track of those files.

takeaways.technique: Runtime code execution instead of large tool surface
takeaways.what_they_do: At query time the engine writes and executes code (Jupyter-like) to fetch/transform data, iterating until correct, rather than giving the agent a huge set of tool definitions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We went down from having something like 150,000 tokens to give our agents all the tooling they need to less than a thousand tokens.
takeaways.numbers: ~150,000 tokens -> <1,000 tokens of interface spec; 77-90% token reduction common; 20-77% faster

takeaways.what_they_do: The query API requires the caller to pass a token/dollar/time budget so the system can choose between a quick answer and an exhaustive search.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's really important for you to give us the budget in tokens or in dollars. how much time you want us to invest

takeaways.what_they_do: When a fact changes (e.g. new CEO), the layer immediately overrides stale documents so retrieval doesn't return outdated info.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the company replaces its CEO, the very next day, everybody in the company knows who the CEO is... every rag search will tell you otherwise.

takeaways.what_they_do: Separate knowledge contexts per domain (HR, ops, engineering), each owned by the relevant domain experts who keep it aligned.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's a good practice to have the domain experts in the company own those and have being able to interact with them
